front: Le pouvoir d'achat est la première préoccupation des Français.
pronunciation: [luh poo-vwahr dah-SHAH eh lah pruh-myehr pray-oh-kü-pah-SYOHN day frahn-SEH]
back: Purchasing power is French people's top concern.
context: 'Le pouvoir d'achat' comes up in almost every French political debate.

front: L'inflation a fait grimper les prix de l'alimentation.
pronunciation: [lan-flah-SYOHN ah feh gran-pay lay pree duh lah-lee-mahn-tah-SYOHN]
back: Inflation has pushed up food prices.
context: 'Grimper' = to climb, rise.

front: Les syndicats ont appelé à une grève nationale.
pronunciation: [lay san-dee-KAH ohn tah-puh-lay ah ün grev nah-syoh-NAL]
back: The unions have called a national strike.
context: 'Un syndicat' = trade union. Strikes are a frequent, legal form of protest in France.

front: La réforme des retraites a repoussé l'âge légal de départ à soixante-quatre ans.
pronunciation: [lah ray-form day ruh-TRET ah ruh-poo-say lahzh lay-gal duh day-par ah swah-sahnt-KAT-ruh AHN]
back: The pension reform raised the legal retirement age to 64.
context: The 2023 reform moved it from 62 to 64 and sparked months of protests.

front: Le gouvernement a eu recours au 49.3 pour faire passer le texte.
pronunciation: [luh goo-vehr-nuh-mahn ah ü ruh-koor oh kah-rahnt-nuhf-TRWAH poor fehr pah-say luh TEKST]
back: The government used Article 49.3 to push the bill through.
context: Article 49.3 of the Constitution lets a bill pass without a vote unless the government is toppled.

front: Le SMIC a été revalorisé en janvier.
pronunciation: [luh SMEEK ah ay-tay ruh-vah-loh-ree-ZAY ahn zhahn-VYAY]
back: The minimum wage was increased in January.
context: 'Le SMIC' = the statutory minimum wage. 'Revaloriser' = to raise (a wage, a pension).

front: Le taux de chômage reste autour de sept pour cent.
pronunciation: [luh toh duh shoh-MAHZH rest oh-toor duh set poor SAHN]
back: The unemployment rate stays around seven percent.
context: 'Le taux de chômage' = unemployment rate. 'Autour de' = around.

front: Les jeunes peinent à trouver un logement abordable.
pronunciation: [lay ZHUHN pen ah troo-vay an lozh-mahn ah-bor-DAH-bluh]
back: Young people struggle to find affordable housing.
context: 'Peiner à' = to struggle to. 'Abordable' = affordable.

front: La crise du logement touche surtout les grandes villes.
pronunciation: [lah kreez dü lozh-MAHN toosh sür-too lay grahnd VEEL]
back: The housing crisis mainly affects the big cities.
context: 'Toucher' = to affect.

front: Dans certaines régions rurales, il y a des déserts médicaux.
pronunciation: [dahn sehr-ten ray-zhyohn rü-RAL, eel yah day day-zehr may-dee-KOH]
back: In some rural areas, there are 'medical deserts'.
context: 'Un désert médical' = an area with too few doctors.

front: La population française vieillit.
pronunciation: [lah poh-pü-lah-syohn frahn-sez vyeh-YEE]
back: The French population is aging.
context: 'Vieillir' = to grow old.

front: La France produit l'essentiel de son électricité grâce au nucléaire.
pronunciation: [lah frahns proh-dwee leh-sahn-syel duh sohn nay-lek-tree-see-TAY grahs oh nü-klay-EHR]
back: France produces most of its electricity from nuclear power.
context: Nuclear provides roughly two-thirds of French electricity, more than in almost any other country.

front: La transition énergétique est un enjeu majeur.
pronunciation: [lah trahn-zee-syohn ay-nehr-zhay-TEEK eh tan nahn-zhuh ma-ZHUHR]
back: The energy transition is a major issue.
context: 'Un enjeu' = an issue, what is at stake. Very frequent in news French.

front: Il faut réduire les émissions de gaz à effet de serre.
pronunciation: [eel foh ray-dweer lay zay-mee-syohn duh gahz ah eh-feh duh SEHR]
back: We need to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.
context: 'Le gaz à effet de serre' = greenhouse gas.

front: De plus en plus de villes créent des zones à faibles émissions.
pronunciation: [duh plü zahn plü duh VEEL kray day zohn ah feh-bluh zay-mee-SYOHN]
back: More and more cities are creating low-emission zones.
context: 'ZFE' = zone à faibles émissions: older polluting cars are banned.

front: Le vélo a connu un véritable essor à Paris.
pronunciation: [luh vay-LOH ah koh-nü an vay-ree-tah-bluh eh-SOR ah pah-REE]
back: Cycling has really taken off in Paris.
context: 'Un essor' = a boom, rapid growth.

front: La canicule de l'été dernier a battu des records.
pronunciation: [lah kah-nee-kül duh lay-tay dehr-NYAY ah bah-tü day ruh-KOR]
back: Last summer's heatwave broke records.
context: 'Battre un record' = to break a record.

front: Le mouvement des gilets jaunes est né d'une hausse du prix du carburant.
pronunciation: [luh moov-mahn day zhee-leh ZHOHN eh nay dün ohs dü pree dü kar-bü-RAHN]
back: The yellow vest movement began with a rise in fuel prices.
context: In 2018. 'Une hausse' = a rise; 'une baisse' = a fall.

front: Les manifestants défilent de la République à la Nation.
pronunciation: [lay mah-nee-fes-TAHN day-feel duh lah ray-pü-BLEEK ah lah nah-SYOHN]
back: The protesters are marching from République to Nation.
context: Classic Paris protest route between two squares. 'Défiler' = to march.

front: La laïcité est un principe fondamental de la République.
pronunciation: [lah lah-ee-see-TAY eh tan pran-seep fohn-dah-mahn-TAL duh lah ray-pü-BLEEK]
back: Secularism is a fundamental principle of the Republic.
context: 'La laïcité': separation of religion and state, established by the 1905 law.

front: Le débat sur l'immigration divise profondément la société.
pronunciation: [luh day-bah sür lee-mee-grah-SYOHN dee-veez proh-fohn-day-MAHN lah soh-syay-TAY]
back: The debate on immigration deeply divides society.
context: 'Diviser' = to divide.

front: Les inégalités entre Paris et la province se creusent.
pronunciation: [lay zee-nay-gah-lee-TAY ahn-truh pah-REE ay lah proh-VANS suh KRUHZ]
back: Inequalities between Paris and the rest of France are widening.
context: 'Se creuser' (to deepen) = to widen (a gap).

front: Le télétravail a transformé la vie de nombreux salariés.
pronunciation: [luh tay-lay-trah-VAHY ah trahns-for-may lah vee duh nohm-bruh sah-lah-RYAY]
back: Remote work has transformed the lives of many employees.
context: 'Un salarié' = an employee.

front: Beaucoup de citadins se sont installés à la campagne après la pandémie.
pronunciation: [boh-koo duh see-tah-DAN suh sohn tan-stah-lay ah lah kahm-PAN-yuh ah-preh lah pahn-day-MEE]
back: Many city dwellers moved to the countryside after the pandemic.
context: 'Un citadin' = a city dweller.

front: L'égalité salariale entre les femmes et les hommes n'est pas encore atteinte.
pronunciation: [lay-gah-lee-tay sah-lah-RYAL ahn-truh lay fam ay lay ZUM neh pah zahn-kor ah-TANT]
back: Equal pay between women and men has not yet been achieved.
context: 'Atteindre' = to reach, achieve → atteint(e).

front: La loi impose la parité sur les listes électorales.
pronunciation: [lah lwah an-pohz lah pah-ree-TAY sür lay leest ay-lek-toh-RAL]
back: The law requires gender parity on electoral lists.
context: 'La parité' = equal numbers of women and men.

front: Les Jeux olympiques de Paris en 2024 ont été un grand succès populaire.
pronunciation: [lay zhuh oh-lan-PEEK duh pah-REE ahn duh meel van-KAT ohn tay-TAY an grahn sük-seh poh-pü-LEHR]
back: The 2024 Paris Olympics were a great popular success.
context: 'Un succès' = a success (not 'succession').

front: L'économie française repose en grande partie sur les services.
pronunciation: [lay-koh-noh-mee frahn-SEZ ruh-pohz ahn grahnd par-TEE sür lay sehr-VEES]
back: The French economy relies largely on services.
context: 'Reposer sur' = to rely on. 'En grande partie' = largely.

front: Le tourisme représente une part importante du PIB.
pronunciation: [luh too-REEZM ruh-pray-zahnt ün par an-por-TAHNT dü pay-ee-BAY]
back: Tourism represents a significant share of GDP.
context: 'Le PIB' (produit intérieur brut) = GDP. France is one of the most visited countries in the world.

front: La dette publique inquiète les économistes.
pronunciation: [lah det pü-BLEEK an-KYET lay zay-koh-noh-MEEST]
back: The public debt worries economists.
context: 'La dette publique' = national debt.

front: Les agriculteurs protestent contre la baisse de leurs revenus.
pronunciation: [lay zah-gree-kül-TUHR proh-test kohn-truh lah bes duh luhr ruh-vuh-NÜ]
back: Farmers are protesting against the fall in their income.
context: 'Les revenus' = income.

front: Le gaspillage alimentaire est désormais interdit dans les supermarchés.
pronunciation: [luh gas-pee-yahzh ah-lee-mahn-TEHR eh day-zor-meh zan-tehr-DEE dahn lay sü-pehr-mar-SHAY]
back: Food waste is now banned in supermarkets.
context: Since 2016 French supermarkets must donate unsold food. 'Désormais' = from now on.

front: Le tri des déchets est obligatoire.
pronunciation: [luh tree day day-SHEH eh toh-blee-gah-TWAHR]
back: Sorting waste is compulsory.
context: 'Les déchets' = waste. 'La poubelle jaune' = recycling bin in many towns.

front: Le gouvernement veut relancer la croissance.
pronunciation: [luh goo-vehr-nuh-MAHN vuh ruh-lahn-say lah krwah-SAHNS]
back: The government wants to boost growth.
context: 'Relancer' = to revive, boost. 'La croissance' = growth.

front: Les élections législatives ont abouti à une Assemblée sans majorité absolue.
pronunciation: [lay zay-lek-syohn lay-zhees-lah-TEEV ohn tah-boo-tee ah ün nah-sahm-blay sahn mah-zhoh-ree-tay ab-soh-LÜ]
back: The legislative elections produced an Assembly with no absolute majority.
context: 'Aboutir à' = to result in. 'L'Assemblée nationale' = lower house of Parliament.

front: Le président de la République est élu pour cinq ans.
pronunciation: [luh pray-zee-dahn duh lah ray-pü-BLEEK eh tay-LÜ poor san KAHN]
back: The President of the Republic is elected for five years.
context: 'Le quinquennat' = the five-year term (since 2002).

front: Le Premier ministre dirige l'action du gouvernement.
pronunciation: [luh pruh-myay mee-NEES-truh dee-reezh lak-syohn dü goo-vehr-nuh-MAHN]
back: The Prime Minister directs the government's work.
context: France has both a president and a prime minister.

front: Les Français sont très attachés à leur système de santé.
pronunciation: [lay frahn-SEH sohn treh zah-tah-shay ah luhr sees-tem duh sahn-TAY]
back: French people are very attached to their healthcare system.
context: 'Être attaché à' = to be attached to, value.

front: La Sécurité sociale rembourse une grande partie des soins.
pronunciation: [lah say-kü-ree-tay soh-SYAL rahm-boors ün grahnd par-tee day SWAN]
back: Social Security reimburses a large share of healthcare costs.
context: 'La Sécu' (informal). 'Les soins' = healthcare, treatment.

front: Le modèle social français coûte cher, mais il protège.
pronunciation: [luh moh-del soh-syal frahn-SEH koot SHEHR, meh eel proh-TEZH]
back: The French social model is expensive, but it protects people.
context: A sentence that sums up a recurring national debate.

front: L'abstention a atteint un niveau record.
pronunciation: [lab-stahn-syohn ah ah-tan tan nee-voh ruh-KOR]
back: Abstention reached a record level.
context: 'L'abstention' = not voting.

front: Les jeunes s'engagent pour le climat.
pronunciation: [lay zhuhn sahn-gahzh poor luh klee-MAH]
back: Young people are getting involved in climate action.
context: 'S'engager' = to commit, get involved.

front: La filière automobile se tourne vers l'électrique.
pronunciation: [lah fee-lyehr oh-toh-moh-BEEL suh toorn vehr lay-lek-TREEK]
back: The car industry is turning to electric vehicles.
context: 'Une filière' = an industry sector, supply chain.

front: Le prix de l'énergie pèse sur les ménages modestes.
pronunciation: [luh pree duh lay-nehr-ZHEE pez sür lay may-nahzh moh-DEST]
back: Energy prices weigh on low-income households.
context: 'Un ménage' = a household. 'Modeste' = low-income.

front: Les banlieues souffrent d'un manque de services publics.
pronunciation: [lay bahn-LYUH soofr dan mahnk duh sehr-vees pü-BLEEK]
back: The suburbs suffer from a lack of public services.
context: 'Les banlieues' often refers to disadvantaged suburban areas around big cities.

front: Le gouvernement a annoncé un plan de rénovation énergétique des logements.
pronunciation: [luh goo-vehr-nuh-mahn ah ah-noh-say an plahn duh ray-noh-vah-syohn ay-nehr-zhay-TEEK day lozh-MAHN]
back: The government announced a plan to make housing more energy-efficient.
context: 'Les passoires thermiques' (thermal sieves) = badly insulated homes.

front: Selon un sondage récent, la majorité des Français est pessimiste.
pronunciation: [suh-lohn an sohn-dahzh ray-SAHN, lah mah-zhoh-ree-tay day frahn-seh eh peh-see-MEEST]
back: According to a recent poll, most French people are pessimistic.
context: 'Un sondage' = a poll. French people often rank as pessimistic in international surveys.

front: Le débat public est de plus en plus polarisé.
pronunciation: [luh day-bah pü-BLEEK eh duh plü zahn plü poh-lah-ree-ZAY]
back: Public debate is increasingly polarized.
context: 'Polarisé' = polarized.

front: Les associations jouent un rôle clé dans l'aide aux plus démunis.
pronunciation: [lay zah-soh-syah-SYOHN zhoo tan rohl KLAY dahn led oh plü day-mü-NEE]
back: Charities play a key role in helping the most disadvantaged.
context: 'Les Restos du cœur' is a famous charity founded by Coluche in 1985. 'Démuni' = destitute.

front: La France reste l'un des pays les plus visités au monde.
pronunciation: [lah frahns rest lan day pay-EE lay plü vee-zee-TAY oh MOHND]
back: France remains one of the most visited countries in the world.
context: 'Au monde' = in the world.
